is something like parsing a large binary format, compression, decompression, geometry boolean operations, pathfinding, constraint solving, physics simulation, audio processing, font shaping, PDF processing, image codec logic, graph layout, triangulation, or running a database engine like SQLite in the browser. These are often good Wasm candidates if the workload is large enough and can be isolated from the UI. But they should not automatically be Wasm. First you should check whether optimized JavaScript plus a Web Worker is enough. Wasm becomes attractive when the computation is genuinely hot, stable, low-level, and can operate on buffers, typed arrays, numbers, or compact data structures.

is something like rendering a 3D scene, drawing thousands of particles, applying lighting, rasterizing textured meshes, running fragment shaders, doing post-processing, drawing large animated visualizations, or handling shader-based effects. That belongs in WebGL or WebGPU because the GPU is built for wide parallel numeric work over vertices, pixels, textures, and buffers. JavaScript or Wasm may prepare the data, but the expensive parallel rendering should happen in shaders.

TCP packets are split into segments during transmission. Because TCP guarantees the sequence of packets, the server must receive an acknowledgement from the client in the form of an ACK packet after sending a certain number of segments
If the server waits for an ACK after each segment, that will result in frequent ACKs from the client and may increase transmission time, even in the case of a low-load network

On the other hand sending too many segments at once can lead to the problem that in a busy network the client will not be able to receive the segments and will just keep responding with ACKs for a long time
